content:
For a vase with a constant base area,  
\[
\text{volume}=\text{base area}\times\text{water height}.
\]
So for the same amount of water, a larger base area gives a lower water level, and a smaller base area gives a higher water level.

From the front view, the vases have the same width, so their top-view widths are the same. Their depths determine their base areas.

Compare the water levels:
- Vase II has the highest water level but contains less water than I, so its base area/depth must be the smallest.
- Vases I and III both contain 4 L, but III has the lowest water level, so its base area/depth must be the largest.
- Therefore, the depths must satisfy:
\[
\text{II}<\text{I}<\text{III}.
\]

Among the choices, only image (A) has the same width for all three and depths ordered II < I < III.

\[
\boxed{\text{(A)}}
\]
